takeaways: The main language of each page can be determined by software. On the web this is the lang attribute on the page; in apps it is the app or content language.
Screen readers use it to choose the right voice and pronunciation. Without it, a Spanish page may be read with English rules and become nonsense.
Browsers and translation tools also use it, for example to offer translation or to hyphenate words correctly.
Developers set the code. Designers and content teams decide which language each page and template is in, and say so at handoff, especially on multilingual products.
failures: Translated pages that still declare English
No page language set at all
A shared template whose language is fixed to the original market
check: List every locale your product ships, and the language code for each.
Check that each translated template or screen is labelled with its language in the file.
In the build, inspect the page language, or listen with a screen reader for the right accent.

quiz.question: Your product launches in Canada with English and French versions built from one template. What do you hand off?
options: Nothing. Screen readers detect the language automatically
Set the template’s language to English, since it is the source design
A note that each page’s language must match its locale: en-CA for English, fr-CA for French
quiz.why: Screen readers do not reliably guess the language, and a fixed English setting makes French pages sound wrong. The language must follow the content of each page.

spec: Give the language code for each locale and template.
Note that the page language changes with the content, not with the design source.
For apps, state which language setting the content follows: the device, the account or a picker.
review: Which language does each version of this page declare?
Who updates the language when we add a new locale?
Have we heard this page through a screen reader in each language?
tradeoff: Localization often happens after design handoff, so nobody owns the language setting. Make it part of the locale checklist, so whoever adds a language also sets it.
system: Make the page language a required property of the page template, set from the locale.
pitch: One missing attribute can make a whole page sound like gibberish to a screen reader user. It takes seconds to set.
